title: for Loops and Counter-Controlled Iteration
learningObjectives: Explain the key idea in for loops and counter-controlled iteration.
Identify the relevant syntax and rules.
Trace each example and predict the result.
Apply the concept in a small program.
Avoid a common mistake related to this topic.

understand.concept: A for loop places initialization, continuation condition and update expression together. It is commonly used when iteration follows a counter or known range. The loop variable's scope is usually limited to the loop.
understand.whyItMatters: for loops compactly express counted repetition and reduce the chance of forgetting an update step.
understand.analogy: Think of this as a control or calculation rule that tells a program how to handle a particular situation consistently.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is only a starting point; C++ syntax, types and execution rules determine actual behaviour.
understand.explain:
## Loop header
The `for` header has initialization, condition and update separated by semicolons. Initialization runs once; the condition is checked before each iteration; update runs after the body.

## Counter patterns
Use increasing or decreasing counters and carefully choose inclusive or exclusive boundaries.

## Range-based for
For collections such as arrays and vectors, a range-based for can iterate over each element without manually managing an index.

examples.title: Count 1 to 5
examples.explanation: Initialization, condition and increment define the count.

examples.title: Even numbers
examples.code: for (int n{2}; n <= 10; n += 2) { std::cout << n << ' '; }

examples.title: Reverse counting
examples.explanation: The counter moves toward the stopping condition.

examples.title: Sum in loop
examples.code: int sum{0};\nfor (int i{1}; i <= 5; ++i) { sum += i; }\nstd::cout << sum;
examples.explanation: The loop computes the sum of 1 through 5.

examples.title: Range-based for
examples.code: int values[]{4, 7, 9};\nfor (int value : values) { std::cout << value << ' '; }
examples.explanation: The range-based loop visits each element.
